<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="TE(æ)A,ea." /></noinclude>{{c|CHAPTER XII.

{{sc|Causation.}}}}

{{smaller block|"Every Cause has its Effect; every Effect has its Cause; everything happens according to Law; Chance is but a name for Law not recognized; there are many planes of causation, but nothing escapes the Law."—''The Kybalion.''}}

The great Sixth Hermetic Principle—the Principle of Cause and Effect—embodies the truth that Law pervades the Universe; that nothing happens by Chance; that Chance is merely a term indicating cause existing but not recognized or perceived; that phenomena is continuous, without break or exception.

The Principle of Cause and Effect underlies all scientific thought, ancient and modern, and was enunciated by the Hermetic Teachers in the earliest days. While many and varied disputes between the<noinclude>{{c|{{sm|171}}}}</noinclude>
